data.description:
## Context / Problem

Operators who run rebar's gate operations through an OpenAI-compatible gateway (set via
`llm.base_url`) have that gateway reporting to an observability backend such as Langfuse.
rebar sends no request metadata, so every gate call arrives anonymous: it cannot be
attributed to rebar, grouped into one trace per gate run, or tied back to the ticket and
signed verdict that produced it.

rebar already reserved the field for this. `src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` and
`src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` each declare `trace_id` as
`["string","null"]`, described as "Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled; null
otherwise", while `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:259` and `:719` pass `trace_id=None`
unconditionally. The correlation identity was specified and never implemented.

The existing OTLP path (`src/rebar/llm/tracing.py:196`, `setup_tracing`) is a different
mechanism and is unchanged by this epic: it exports rebar's own spans directly to Langfuse.
This epic serves the deployment where the gateway, not rebar, feeds the backend.

## Approach

Add one generic, operator-configured request-header surface on `LLMConfig`, delivered
through pydantic-ai's `ModelSettings.extra_headers`, whose values may interpolate
environment variables (`${env:VAR}`) and rebar-supplied per-run values (`${run:trace_id}`,
`${run:ticket_id}`, `${run:operation}`, `${run:run_id}`).

Rationale for this shape:

- **One generic dict beats named per-vendor knobs.** A dedicated "trace header name" field
  would force rebar to ship a vendor default, hard-coding one gateway's dialect. A generic
  dict with substitution carries LiteLLM's `x-litellm-trace-id`, Helicone's
  `Helicone-Session-Id`, or an internal gateway's own names equally well. rebar ships no
  vendor header name in code or defaults; vendor names appear only as documentation
  examples, keeping the feature portable across supported client shapes.
- **`ModelSettings.extra_headers` beats patching httpx clients.** It is upstream-supported
  (`pydantic_ai/settings.py`, documented for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Google and others)
  and rebar already has a pure assembly seam at `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:338`
  (`build_model_settings`) feeding `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:567`. Patching transport instead
  would require touching two separate httpx constructions
  (`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:295` and `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:155`) and would
  still miss non-httpx providers.
- **Static and per-run headers are one feature, not two.** A constant header is a dict entry
  without a placeholder; per-run correlation is a dict entry with one. One code path, one
  test surface.

Header values are a credential-bearing surface: both vendor SDKs merge caller headers last,
so a caller-supplied `Authorization` silently displaces the real key. Validation and
redaction are therefore delivered scope, not follow-on work.

## Out of scope

No rebar-owned root span, no unification of rebar's own OTLP spans with the gateway's
records, and no W3C `traceparent` injection. The 32-hex lowercase id format is chosen so
later work can carry a real OTel trace id without a schema or format migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An operator can configure arbitrary request headers for gate LLM calls without editing
      rebar source, and no gateway vendor's header name appears in rebar's shipped code or
      defaults; checked by a test asserting the shipped default is empty and by a test
      asserting no vendor header-name constant exists under `src/rebar/llm/`.
- [ ] A header value can reference an environment variable so a gateway credential is never
      required in a committed config file; checked by a test resolving `${env:VAR}` from a
      monkeypatched environment.
- [ ] All LLM calls within one gate run carry the same correlation value, and two runs carry
      different ones; checked by a test capturing headers across the calls of one simulated
      run.
- [ ] A produced gate verdict names the correlation value in its existing `trace_id` field
      instead of `null`; checked by asserting `trace_id` on a produced verdict and validating
      it against `review_result.schema.json`.
- [ ] A configured header value never appears in logs, diagnostics, or the
      `provider_provenance` record written into verdicts and sidecars; checked by a test
      asserting a sentinel value is absent from captured log output and from the serialized
      provenance record.
- [ ] Header names and values that could forge authentication or inject protocol bytes are
      rejected at config resolution with a named error; checked by parametrized tests over
      the rejected set.

## Child decomposition

- A **configuration** child owns the `headers` field, its resolution across the CLI, env and
  file layers, `${env:...}` interpolation, and the name/value validation that rejects
  authentication and protocol-injection headers. It delivers criteria 1, 2 and 6.
- A **run-correlation** child owns minting the per-run identity at the gate run boundaries
  and populating the verdict `trace_id` field. It delivers criterion 4.
- A **delivery** child owns `${run:...}` interpolation and placing resolved headers on the
  wire through `extra_headers`, gated on a configured `base_url`, together with the
  redaction guarantee at every emission point. It delivers criteria 3 and 5, and depends on
  both children above.
- A **documentation** child records the operator-facing recipe and security guidance, and
  depends on the delivery child.
data.title: Configurable LLM request headers with per-run correlation for gateway observability
